Lemma
[local liftability of a curve through a local homeomorphism]

1. ch7:3.3Let $f:M\to N$ be a local homeomorphism and $c:[0,1]\to N$ a continuous curve.

  1. For every $s$ and every point $q\in M$ over $c(s)$ (that is, $f(q)=c(s)$) the curve $c$ lifts through $q$ on a nondegenerate interval to the right: there is a continuous $\bar c:[s,s+\varepsilon ]\to M$ with $\bar c(s)=q$ and $f\circ \bar c=c$.

  2. Consequently, if $c$ lifts to a continuous $\bar c:[a,t]\to M$ with $f\circ \bar c=c$, then the lift extends to $[a,t+\delta ]$ for some $\delta >0$: the set of parameters over which $c$ lifts starting from a fixed initial point is open to the right.

Proof

\sketch A local inverse of $f$ near any point over $c(s)$ lifts $c$ on a small interval. Applying this at the endpoint of a partial lift extends the lift to the right.

□
